summary: GLP-1 radar for 29 Sept 2026, during EASD 2026 in Milan (28 Sept–2 Oct). Most of the new news is coming out of EASD. The strongest openings are: (1) the WashU study of 333,000 veterans with type 2 diabetes, which linked stopping GLP-1 treatment to a higher risk of heart attack, stroke and death; (2) a Nordic registry study that found no link between semaglutide and pancreatic cancer, which works as a myth-bust; (3) retatrutide's TRIUMPH-2 phase 3 diabetes results, due at an EASD symposium on 30 Sept. That one is at the earliest stage, but it needs strict wording that the drug is not approved and should never be bought as a research chemical; (4) new analyses of the Foundayo (orforglipron) pill, including similar weight loss across all menopause stages. Common questions remain steady and get a fresh hook here: hair loss (the BMJ study from July plus Guardian coverage this week), sleep apnea vs CPAP, and non-responders. The SELECT mediation topic has now appeared in 6 snapshots and is close to peaking, so it's only worth doing with a 'what else explains it' angle. Side-effect signals (eye stroke/NAION, period changes) are rated caution: they come from FDA adverse-event report (FAERS) analyses and must be worded as signals, not proof. One item is rejected: MindBodyGreen-style 'GLP-1 microdosing in perimenopause' content goes against our guardrails. Across all EASD stories, date-hedge every claim ('presented at EASD, full paper not yet published as of Sept 2026'), flag company-funded and indirect comparisons, and don't offer any advice on stopping or switching.

candidates.topic: Stopping GLP-1 medicines linked to higher heart attack, stroke and death risk: WashU study of 333,000+ US veterans with type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: 'The heart protection builds slowly and fades fast.' Explain what the study found: about 22% higher relative risk after 2 years off treatment, and benefits not fully restored when treatment restarted. Frame it as a reason to plan any change with your prescriber, never as 'don't stop'. Make clear it's observational and covers veterans with type 2 diabetes, and give relative vs absolute risk.
keywords: what happens when you stop GLP-1
candidates.why_now: Press release came out ~20 Sept. Local Scripps/ABC stations syndicated it on 29 Sept, so it's now spreading into mainstream news. People searching 'what happens when you stop' are a huge, anxious audience, and few creators give careful, prescriber-first explanations.

evidence.signal: 333,000+ veterans with T2D; interruption linked to higher MACE; 22% higher relative risk at 2 years off
Science-press pickup
Mainstream TV syndication across many local stations
National coverage of risks of stopping

candidates.topic: Semaglutide not linked to pancreatic cancer: regulator-mandated Nordic registry study (97,464 matched pairs, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Myth-bust with a concrete number: 'Nearly 100,000 matched pairs, and no increase in pancreatic cancer.' Name the population (adults with type 2 diabetes in Denmark, Sweden and Norway, compared with insulin, sulfonylurea or SGLT2 starters). Disclose Novo Nordisk funding and the observational design. Can pair with the Sept 2026 J Pers Med global cohort on pancreatitis.
candidates.why_now: Medscape and Medical Xpress covered it on 28 Sept, ahead of the EASD presentation this week. 'Does Ozempic cause cancer' is a constant search, and this is the newest large reassuring dataset. Health creators haven't picked it up yet.

evidence.signal: 97,464 matched pairs; Novo-funded post-authorization safety study; EASD 2026
Science news pickup 28 Sept
Global propensity-matched cohort: GLP-1 RAs not associated with pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer in T2D

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2: phase 3 results in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity presented at EASD on 30 Sept (topline: up to 20.8% average weight loss at 80 weeks)
candidates.angle: 'What is a triple agonist?' Explain GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon simply, and put the phase 3 numbers in context next to STEP and SURMOUNT. Be clear that 'up to' means the highest dose, results are topline/company-reported, and it's NOT approved. Warn clearly that anything sold online as 'retatrutide' is an unregulated research chemical.
candidates.why_now: Full data comes at the EASD symposium on 30 Sept, tomorrow. Lilly's CEO is calling retatrutide the next growth driver. Search interest spikes with each data readout, and gray-market interest is high, so a responsible explainer is valuable.

evidence.signal: Foundayo, retatrutide and eloraTZP data at EASD 2026
Retatrutide diabetes results lead EASD opening
Retatrutide T2D + obesity trial registry

candidates.topic: Oral GLP-1 pill orforglipron (Foundayo): similar weight loss in pre-, peri- and postmenopausal women (ATTAIN-1/ATTAIN-2 post-hoc)
candidates.angle: 'Does menopause blunt GLP-1 results?' In ATTAIN-1 (17.2 mg arm), women lost 12.8% (pre), 14.4% (peri) and 14.1% (post) at 72 weeks. Label it post-hoc and give the separate ATTAIN-2 (T2D) numbers. Add the evidence-based protein and strength-training piece for muscle and bone in midlife.
candidates.why_now: Medical Xpress, News-Medical and Times of India covered it 26–29 Sept. Everyday Health and MindBodyGreen are running GLP-1 + menopause pieces. Our audience of women aged 45–65 is actively searching this, and there's little careful video coverage.

evidence.signal: Similar weight loss across three menopausal stages
Up to 14%; stage-specific numbers

candidates.topic: GLP-1 and hair loss: how common it really is (The BMJ, July 2026) and why rapid weight loss matters
candidates.angle: Calm, practical myth-bust: the BMJ found a modest increase, mostly non-scarring shedding (often telogen effluvium) that usually grows back. Cover what's thought to drive it (fast weight loss, low protein intake) and when to see a clinician. Population: adults with type 2 diabetes in the cohort data.
candidates.why_now: The Guardian (28 Sept) and Times of India ran explainers, which refreshes an always-high search. Most existing videos are anecdotal, so an evidence-first take stands out.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 users with T2D more likely to have hair loss vs other diabetes drugs

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only ~20% of semaglutide's heart benefit (SELECT mediation, European Heart Journal): what else might be doing the work
candidates.angle: Differentiated follow-up now that it's near peak: 'So if not weight, then what?' Cover the candidate mechanisms (inflammation/CRP, blood pressure, lipids, direct vessel effects) while saying researchers can't fully explain it yet. Population: adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity, without diabetes.
keywords: why does semaglutide protect the heart
candidates.why_now: Seen in 6 snapshots at momentum 70–76. News-Medical and Medical Daily re-covered it on 28–29 Sept. It's still being searched, but coverage is saturating, so only go ahead with a mechanism-focused angle.

candidates.topic: Oral GLP-1 face-off: Foundayo (orforglipron) vs oral semaglutide in type 2 diabetes, a new indirect comparison
candidates.angle: 'Which GLP-1 pill?' Explain what an indirect treatment comparison can and can't tell you: no head-to-head trial, Lilly-sponsored, T2D population. Compare how each pill is taken (no food/water rules vs empty stomach). Frame it as questions to bring to a prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Lilly's PR on 29 Sept is being picked up by finance and pharma outlets. Consumer interest in GLP-1 pills is rising since the oral Wegovy (Dec 2025) and Foundayo (Apr 2026) approvals. Few neutral explainers exist.

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and sleep apnea: they cut breathing interruptions, but CPAP remains the most effective therapy (JAMA Otolaryngology review)
candidates.angle: 'Teammates, not rivals.' Explain why weight and tongue fat matter to sleep apnea, and why anatomy is also part of it. Mention that tirzepatide is FDA-approved for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. Never suggest dropping CPAP.
candidates.why_now: Nexstar syndicated The Hill story across dozens of local stations (26–28 Sept), and Yahoo Health ran 'Should you take a GLP-1 for OSA?'. It's a big overlap audience with little evidence-led video coverage.

candidates.topic: 'Why isn't my GLP-1 working?': 10–15% of trial participants lose less than 5% of body weight
candidates.angle: Encouraging and non-judgmental: what 'non-responder' means, trial numbers (about 1 in 7 on semaglutide and 1 in 11 on tirzepatide below 5%), why response varies, and that weight loss isn't the only benefit. End with 'bring this to your prescriber', with no switching or dose advice.
keywords: why am I not losing weight on wegovy
candidates.why_now: DongA Science ran it on 27 Sept, and the Medscape 'Navigating GLP-1 switches' guide came out 29 Sept. Frustrated users search this constantly, and it fits our concrete-number myth-bust hypothesis.

candidates.topic: CagriSema beat tirzepatide 5 mg on weight loss in REIMAGINE 5 (adults with type 2 diabetes, 12.4% vs 9.1% at 60 weeks)
candidates.angle: 'Read the fine print': explain amylin + semaglutide simply, and point out that the comparator was the lowest tirzepatide dose (5 mg), which is key context for the 'beats Zepbound' headlines. Topline company data; HbA1c similar (1.71 vs 1.67 points). Not yet approved.
candidates.why_now: Pharmacy Times, NewsNation and Yahoo Finance headlines 27–28 Sept call it 'outperforms Zepbound'. A misleading-headline correction is timely, and there's an EASD news cycle.

evidence.signal: CagriSema bests tirzepatide in adults with T2D

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and 'eye stroke' (NAION): what the reporting signal shows, and the symptoms to act on
candidates.angle: Calm, factual safety explainer: NAION is rare. The British Journal of Ophthalmology analysis is based on FAERS reports, so it shows a signal, not proven causation. Cover regulators' stance (EMA/MHRA list it as very rare) and the sudden vision changes that need urgent care. No fear framing, no stop advice.
candidates.why_now: A Boston.com lawsuit story (28 Sept), Medical Daily's label-gap piece and Medical Economics (29 Sept) are reviving the topic. Fear-driven content is appearing, so a balanced explainer is needed.

candidates.why_now: Yahoo Health (26 Sept) and others picked it up. It's under-covered, highly relevant to women of reproductive age, and people search it often.
